land.text: Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan, which the Dzungar dossier records as lost to the Qing in 1696

predecessors.note: KM: Abdullah Beg Tarkhan 'ruler of Hami in 1696 after submitting to the Qing as a vassal during the Dzungar-Qing War'; Kumul had sent tribute to the Qing since 1647.

land.text: Jin Shuren 'replaced the khanate' with three provincial districts (Hami, Yihe and Yiwu)

successors.note: The Xinjiang province of the Republic of China.

capitals.name: Kumul (Hami)
capitals.note: KM: the capital was Kumul (Hami), Xinjiang; coordinates from the gazetteer's Hami.

rulers.name: Abdullah Beg
rulers.title: Jasak Tarkhan
rulers.note: Granted the Jasak title in 1696; the page's table starts in 1697.

rulers.name: Bashir
rulers.note: Stayed loyal to the Qing when the Dungan revolt broke out.

rulers.name: Maqsud Shah
rulers.note: Died 6 June 1930, when Jin Shuren replaced the khanate. The page's table goes on with Nasir (1930-1934) and a later Bashir (1934-1949); both come after the abolition and the page says only that Yulbars Khan 'attempted to restore the heir Nasir', so they are claimants, not rulers of the khanate, and are left out.

correction.text: Kumul (Hami), the oasis and prefecture of the Kumul Khanate in eastern Xinjiang, as a 220 km radius round Hami cut to Xinjiang (512 cells, about 129,500 km2)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row (Cliopatria folds the oasis into the Dzungar and then the Qing shape): the Hami oasis as a 120 km radius (about 42,000 km2); KM gives no area and no frontier, so this is a floor. The dzungar-khanate dossier removes 'Hami (Qomul) and the oasis lands east of Turpan' from the Dzungar shape in 1696. Status: a vassal throughout, a Qing banner 1696-1912 and a vassal of the Republic of China 1912-1930 (the ledger's vassal pairs, from the infobox). [Widened fx-42, 2 Nov 2026 (dossier request R098): the disc was 120 km (167 cells) while dzungar-khanate_1696 and its ledger/10 cut a 220 km disc round Hami from the Dzungar shape, leaving a ring of about 390 cells that no state drew from 1696 to 1930. Kumul Khanate page (opened in this run): 'The khanate was located in present-day Hami prefecture of Xinjiang' and Jin Shuren replaced it in 1930 with 'three normal provincial administrative districts Hami, Yihe, and Yiwu'; Hami page: the prefecture-level city covers 137,222 km2 (Yizhou, Yiwu and Barkol), which the 220 km disc (140,865 km2) matches within 3 percent where the 120 km disc held under a third of it. Still a floor-and-ceiling reading: no page gives a frontier.] [Review fx-42, 2 Nov 2026: the 220 km disc is cut to Xinjiang (intersect with the admin-1 Xinjiang) in all nine specs; the bare disc spilled 28 cells into Gansu and 17 into Mongolia's Govi-Altay, outside Hami prefecture ('a prefecture-level city in eastern Xinjiang', Hami page), where the Qing shape (and from 1911 Mongolia) holds them. 512 cells, about 129,500 km2, within 6 percent of the prefecture's 137,222 km2.]

region.text: Kumul (Hami), the oasis of the Kumul Khanate in eastern Xinjiang

ledger.note: 1696: the ruler of Hami submits to the Qing and becomes the first Jasak Tarkhan. Infobox 'Established 1696': Abdullah Beg Tarkhan was granted the title 'ruler of Hami in 1696 after submitting to the Qing as a vassal during the Dzungar-Qing War'; the khanate 'fought against the Dzungar Khanate for the Qing'.

1696: Kumul becomes a banner of the Qing. Infobox status 'Banner of the Qing dynasty (1696–1912)'; Abdullah Beg Tarkhan was 'ruler of Hami in 1696 after submitting to the Qing as a vassal during the Dzungar–Qing War'. Recorded from the vassal's side (kumul-khanate is the vassal, qing-dynasty the suzerain); the suzerain's own dossier should carry the mirror event with counterpart kumul-khanate.

1912: the Qing banner status ends with the dynasty. The infobox closes 'Banner of the Qing dynasty' in 1912; the page has the khanate lasting 'within the Qing dynasty and then the Republic of China'; it gives no month.

region.text: Kumul (Hami): 'Vassal of the Republic of China (1912–1930)'

ledger.note: 1912: the khanate continues as a vassal of the Republic of China. Infobox status 'Vassal of the Republic of China (1912–1930)'; 'The Han Chinese governor of Xinjiang, Yang Zengxin, was a monarchist and tolerated the khanate.' Recorded from the vassal's side (kumul-khanate is the vassal, republic-of-china the suzerain); the suzerain's own dossier should carry the mirror event with counterpart kumul-khanate.

region.text: Kumul (Hami): 'Vassal of the Republic of China (1912–1930)'

ledger.note: 1930: the vassalage ends with the abolition. 'Upon Maqsud Shah's death on 6 June 1930 Jin Shuren replaced the khanate' with three provincial districts (Hami, Yihe and Yiwu).

region.text: Kumul (Hami), the oasis of the Kumul Khanate in eastern Xinjiang

ledger.note: 1930: Jin Shuren abolishes the Kumul Khanate. 'Upon Maqsud Shah's death on 6 June 1930 Jin Shuren replaced the khanate' with three provincial districts (Hami, Yihe and Yiwu); the Kumul Rebellion followed.

wars.name: Kumul Rebellion
wars.outcome: Provoked by the abolition of the khanate in 1930 and Jin Shuren's land seizures: rebellion 'broke out on 20 February 1931' and lasted to July 1934; Yulbars Khan appealed to Ma Zhongying. The rebellion ends in 'Defeat of the Turkic Islamic Republic of East Turkestan'.
wars.note: The rebellion falls after the khanate's end (6 June 1930), so kumul-khanate is named only as the cause and the loyalist cause (Kumul_Khanate: Yulbars Khan 'attempted to restore the heir Nasir'); dates from the Kumul_Rebellion infobox '20 February 1931 - July 1934'. The earlier dates 1930-1930 were wrong: Kumul_Khanate gives no start date. The page does not date any held ground (Ma's forces besieged Kumul in 1931, provincial troops deblockaded it on 30 November 1931), so no zone is drawn; the first-east-turkestan-republic dossier carries the 1933-34 land.

certainty.note: An oasis banner whose limits the page never describes; drawn soft.

sources.title: Kumul Khanate
sources.note: Established 1696 (Abdullah Beg Tarkhan, Jasak), Qing banner to 1912, vassal of the Republic of China 1912-1930, rulers table, abolished on Maqsud Shah's death 6 June 1930.

sources.title: Kumul Rebellion
sources.note: Infobox '20 February 1931 – July 1934'; the 1930 abolition of the wang administration, Jin Shuren's land seizures, Yulbars Khan and Ma Zhongying; Kumul besieged 1931, deblockaded 30 November 1931. Does not mention Nasir or Maqsud Shah.

sources.title: Hami
sources.note: fx-42: area 137,222 km2 (Yizhou District, Yiwu County, Barkol Kazakh Autonomous County); 'Kumul became the center of the Kumul Khanate'.

notes:
Written for batch ia-03-x from one page (KM; budget 1-2 for one shape), revised after review on 2026-10-19 with a second page (Kumul_Rebellion). KM gives no area and no frontier. Review fix: the ledger now carries the khanate's status from KM's infobox as vassal events, 'Banner of the Qing dynasty (1696-1912)' then 'Vassal of the Republic of China (1912-1930)' (qing-dynasty 1696 to 1912; republic-of-china 1912 to 1930/6), so it is not drawn as independent for 234 years. They are written from the vassal's side as the reviewer asked, with the suzerain as counterpart; the schema describes vassal_start as the suzerain's event with the vassal as counterpart, so the qing-dynasty and republic-of-china dossiers (ea-08; neither existed on 2026-10-19) should carry the mirror pair with counterpart kumul-khanate and the orchestrator should decide which side the compiler reads. KM's rulers table lists Nasir (1930-34) and a later Bashir (1934-49) after the abolition; they are left out of identity.rulers as claimants (KM: Yulbars Khan 'attempted to restore the heir Nasir'). The Kumul Rebellion is dated 20 February 1931 to July 1934 by its own page, after the khanate's end.
Fix pass fx-42 (2 Nov 2026), dossier request R098: every Hami disc in this dossier (keyframe, ledger 0-5, predecessor and successor land) is now 220 km instead of 120 km, the same disc that dzungar-khanate ledger/10 and its 1696 keyframe cut from the Dzungar shape, so the ring of about 390 cells round Hami is the khanate's (present-day Hami prefecture, 137,222 km2 on the Hami page).
Review fx-42 (2 Nov 2026): the nine Hami discs are cut to Xinjiang ({intersect: disc, admin1 Xinjiang}), dropping 28 Gansu and 17 Govi-Altay cells that lie outside Hami prefecture (Hami page: 'a prefecture-level city in eastern Xinjiang'); 512 cells remain.
